context: Addition combines quantities. a + b is the sum. This is definitional arithmetic, not a computer-algebra system.
Subtraction removes one quantity from another. a - b is the difference.
Multiplication is repeated addition. a * b is the product.
Division splits a quantity into equal parts. Division by zero is undefined.
An exponent repeats multiplication. a^2 is a squared. a^0 is 1 for nonzero a.
A variable is a symbol that stands for an unknown or changing number, often written as x or y.
An equation says two expressions are equal. Solving it means finding values that make both sides the same.
A triangle is a polygon with three sides. In a flat triangle the interior angles add up to 180 degrees.
A circle is the set of points at a fixed radius from a center. Circumference is pi times the diameter. Area is pi times radius squared.
In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
A derivative is the instantaneous rate of change of a function. It is the slope of the tangent line.
An integral accumulates a quantity. A definite integral is the signed area between a curve and the axis over an interval.
A limit is the value a function approaches as its input approaches some point. Calculus builds on limits.
